newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian court holds off Clabecq bankruptcy.
newsitem.headline: Belgian court holds off Clabecq bankruptcy.

text.p: A Belgian commercial court has ruled against declaring Belgian steel maker Forges de Clabecq bankrupt and has instead appointed two experts, a court spokesman said on Friday.

"Clabecq is not bankrupt...two experts have been appointed and they have to submit a first report to the court by Tuesday, December 24," the court official in the southern town of Nivelles told Reuters. He gave no further details.
Clabecq filed for bankruptcy on Thursday after its majority shareholder, Belgium's southern Walloon region, decided to withdraw its support.
The fate of the loss-making steel firm, which employs 1,700 people, appeared to have been sealed on Wednesday when the European Commission rejected a rescue plan by the Walloon region for Clabecq.

The project involved an offer of 1.5 billion Belgian francs of capital, 700 million francs of credit already granted, the writing-off of debts worth more than 800 million francs and the rescheduling of other borrowings.
The Commission said the subsidies went against EU rules which only allow steel sector aid for environmental reasons, for research and development or for company closure.
Walloon govenrment Minister-President Robert Collignon was quoted on Thursday as saying the government reserved the right to appeal against the Commission's decision to reject its rescue plan.
Collignon hopes that a certain amount of activity could be preserved at Clabecq, notably the blast furnace to supply near-by privately-owned small steel firm Usines Gustave Boel.
